_note: ADR-002. Measured from the 1,492 STIG rules embedded in this build (content/rules_rhel{7,8,9,10}.json), chk and fix text, over lines that begin with a $ or # prompt and then a command. Operators are counted at TOP LEVEL only: text inside single quotes, double quotes, backticks, $( ) and after a backslash is skipped, so awk's ($3>=1000)&&(...) and find's -exec ... \; are not miscounted as shell operators. Regenerate with tests/test_pipeline_stig_shapes.py, which re-derives every number here from the same content and fails if this file has gone stale.
_why: A command corpus that cannot compose cannot express the checks the corpus itself contains. If the closed operator set cannot express a common DISA check, that is a finding about the operator set -- reported here -- and never a reason to widen the set quietly.

out_of_scope.name: command substitution
out_of_scope.why: $( ) and backticks execute a command to produce an argument. That is arbitrary execution by another name, and it is the same refusal as | sh: the product cannot explain, rate or cite a command it will only learn at run time. No operator set will ever express it.

out_of_scope.name: shell loop or function
out_of_scope.why: for/while/function bodies are a shell PROGRAM, not a pipeline. Composing one would mean shipping a shell, which is the thing the tool exists not to be.

known_findings.finding: /dev/null is the single most common redirect target in the corpus (26 of 31 absolute redirect targets), and the blast rule as specified rates any target under /dev/** RED. Implemented as specified and reported rather than carved out: /dev holds both the most harmless target (/dev/null) and the most catastrophic (/dev/sda), so a blanket RED errs safe. A carve-out for /dev/null specifically is a Founder/Marcus decision, not an implementation choice, and quietly adding one would be exactly the declared-discriminator mistake MCR-SEC-022 names.
